newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher, bull spreading noted.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher, bull spreading noted.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed higher with bull spreading noted amid growing concern about harvest delays.
Dealers noted September had moved to a small premium to December as weekend rains slowed harvesting of the U.S. spring wheat crop, lessening hedge-related selling pressure.

September rose sharply late with Cargill Investor Services an aggressive late buyer after a 1.2 million bushel buy-stop was triggered. CIS bought 2.0 million bushels of September on the day, and Benson Quinn bought 1.2 million September. CIS was also the biggest seller of September on the day, at 1.1 million bushels, dealers said.

Dealers said the USDA's weekly crop progress report, due out at 1500 CDT, was expected to show around 20 to 22 percent of spring wheat harvested as of Sunday, up from 10 percent a week earlier. After the close, the USDA reported 22 percent of the spring wheat harvested.
September closed 9-3/4 cents a bushel higher at $3.99. Other months were 5-1/2 to four cents up.
Volume on spring wheat totaled 26.0 million bushels, up from 21.3 million on Friday.
